findings.title: Customer-raised concern about older managers navigating the app — confirmed non-issue
findings.description: Rosa states her only prior worry about the platform was whether older, non-technical store managers could navigate the app. She reports this concern did not materialize: her 58-year-old flagship manager (Teresa) books sessions on her phone without difficulty. No defect or missing capability is described; this is a resolved worry, not a product problem.
findings.quote: The only thing I ever worried about was whether the older managers could navigate the app, and even that turned out fine
findings.severity_reason: No defect exists; purely positive/confirmatory feedback with no impact.
findings.match_note: Not a defect or feature gap — explicitly described as a worry that turned out unfounded; no catalogue match applies.

findings.title: Mobile booking experience confirmed working for phone-only field workforce
findings.description: Rosa reports that store managers successfully book their own sessions entirely from their phones, which matters because her field workforce (bakery managers) never sits at a computer. She describes the app as 'quietly working' with no chasing needed from her side. No problem, defect, or requested change is raised — this is unprompted positive feedback about the mobile experience.
findings.quote: The managers book their own sessions, I'm not chasing anyone, the app works on their phones which matters because none of them sit at a computer.
findings.severity_reason: No defect or gap; purely affirmative feedback with no requested change.
findings.match_note: No catalogue issue applies — customer explicitly confirms the mobile experience meets her needs, nothing to file.

findings.title: Customer wants to overlay engagement data with her own HR turnover data for a board slide
findings.description: Rosa wants to correlate BetterBark engagement numbers with her company's internal turnover data by store to build a board presentation slide. Maya clarifies BetterBark cannot pull the customer's HR turnover data, and Rosa agrees to do the overlay herself using the engagement figures Maya provides plus her own HR records. This is a one-off reporting/analysis favor for a board deck, not a request to change or add a product capability.
findings.quote: I'd bet Teresa's store, high-engagement, is also low-turnover now. That'd be a compelling slide.
findings.severity_reason: No product defect or gap; a one-time analysis request outside the product scope.
findings.match_note: Excluded as a services/reporting favour rather than a product defect or missing capability; not filed against any catalogue issue.
